facts.fact: Lands Minister Hamat Bah said on 4 September 2026 that the government is developing a Land Information System to hold digital records of landholdings across the country, with World Bank-supported consultants working on it and a draft due by end-September, and that land-record archives are being digitised.

systems.owner: Ministry of Lands and Regional Government

facts.fact: The National Land Policy 2026-2035 states that land administration suffers from the absence of a centralised Land Information System and a lack of cadastral data, and calls for a digitalised National Land Administration System.

A National Assembly select committee, reviewing a National Audit Office performance audit, found the entire land administration process paper-based with a fully manual registration system and no centralised database at the Ministry of Lands and Regional Government.

systems.owner: Ministry of Lands and Regional Government

note: Policy launch speech; the digital National Land Administration System is only called for, no system or its absence is stated.

facts.fact: Dr Samba Sowe said the alpha version of the National Land Information System is complete and in testing, and that a company has been contracted to set up a data conversion centre to scan historical land records for it.

systems.owner: Ministry of Lands, Local Government and Religious Affairs

facts.fact: The Standard reports a contracted company is developing the digital land registry, with completion expected in 2027 and digitisation of existing land records among the priorities of a USD 10 million programme.

facts.fact: Minister Hamat Bah said a tender for the National Land Information System attracted nine firms, with evaluation and contract signing expected in early 2026.
